entries.claim_or_test: Anti-Gravity RESEARCH-05 — Mach-effect thruster published tests and null/artifact results (first bite-size literature slice, research docs only)
entries.title: Experimental Null test of a Mach Effect Thruster
entries.what_was_measured: Mach-effect thruster net thrust and its elimination in a null test: thrust removal with two heavy masses at either end of the stack and a central mounting bracket.
entries.population_or_system: Mach Effect Thruster stack: two heavy masses at either end of the stack with a central mounting bracket.
entries.measured_result_quote: Then we show how this thrust can be eliminated by having two heavy masses at either end of the stack with a central mounting bracket... We find the thrust does indeed disappear in the experiment, as predicted.
entries.negatives_or_limits: Null result: thrust disappears in the experiment as predicted (vibration/systematic check). The full-text Sec. 2.2 thrust figure (~1.5 µN) was not verified; only the abstract page was opened.

entries.claim_or_test: Anti-Gravity RESEARCH-05 — Mach-effect thruster published tests and null/artifact results (first bite-size literature slice, research docs only)
entries.title: Experimental Investigation of Mach-Effect Thrusters on Torsion Balances
entries.what_was_measured: Forces from Mach-Effect Thrusters (MEGA drive) on torsion balances, in nN/W, including orientations that should produce zero thrust.
entries.population_or_system: Mach-Effect Thrusters / MEGA drive on torsion balances, TU Dresden replication campaign (Monette, Kössling, Tajmar).
entries.measured_result_quote: Abstract: "It is concluded that the observed effect is a result of coupled vibrations on the torsion balance." Sec. 6/Conclusion: "the forces are much lower than predicted (3 to 30 nN/W), and are present in thruster orientations that should not result in thrust... the effects observed by Woodward using the MEGA drive on a torsion balance can be explained by thermal and vibrational artefacts using Newtonian mechanics."
entries.negatives_or_limits: No confirmed uniaxial thrust; observed forces 3–30 nN/W, orders below claimed µN-level forces, present in orientations that should yield zero thrust; attributed to thermal and vibrational artefacts. Caveats: PDF text truncated mid-Sec. 6; part of the quote appears in Section 7 Conclusion, not Sec. 6; no DOI on the proof PDF.

entries.claim_or_test: Anti-Gravity RESEARCH-05 — Mach-effect thruster published tests and null/artifact results (first bite-size literature slice, research docs only)
entries.title: The SpaceDrive Project - Thrust Balance Development and New Measurements of the Mach-Effect and EMDrive Thrusters
entries.what_was_measured: Thrust-balance test signals for Mach-Effect and EM Drive thrusters; whether signals indicate real thrust.
entries.population_or_system: Mach-Effect and EM Drive thrusters on thrust balances, TU Dresden SpaceDrive project (IAC-18, Bremen 2018).
entries.measured_result_quote: tests "were performed and indicate thermal drifts instead of real thrusts. This needs to be further investigated."
entries.negatives_or_limits: No real thrust observed; measured signals attributed to non-linear thermal drifts rather than thrust. Caveats: no DOI printed on the document; PDF text extraction is page-fragmented with ellipsis gaps.

notes: Only verdict TRUE sources were used, per instructions. S03 (NASA NIAC Phase II Final Report - Mach Effects for In-Space Propulsion: Interstellar Mission) had verify verdict FALSE and was excluded; no new sources were added. For S01 only the abstract was opened, so its full-text ~1.5 µN thrust figure (Sec. 2.2) is not quote-verified. Entry titles are as printed on the opened pages.
